title: Locale Pack
description: A file under cvloom/locales/ supplying the document-facing defaults cvloom would otherwise hardcode in English. Governs the rendered document only — never the terminal.

html_lang.description: Value for <html lang>. Drives WeasyPrint hyphenation and the PDF /Lang metadata that ATS language detection reads.

section_titles.description: Default heading per section key. A profile's section_titles block overrides any of these; that profile block stays the only per-document customization mechanism.

ongoing.description: The open-ended end date, in both directions. Bidirectional by nature: `render` is written into the document by filters.date_range, `accepts` is parsed back out by the chronology lint rule and the JSON Resume export. Both are required together — a pack supplying only one silently degrades the other side.

render.description: Written for an entry with no end date, e.g. 'Present'.

accepts.description: Values recognised as meaning ongoing when read back from data. Matched case-insensitively; include the rendered form.

duration.description: How this locale writes a tenure, e.g. '(2 years 3 months)'. Written after a work date range by filters.duration when a profile sets show_durations. All six keys are required together: a pack with plural words but no singular ones would write '1 years'.

join.description: Placed between the years part and the months part, e.g. ' ' or ' y '.

format.description: Wraps the joined parts. Must contain the {value} placeholder, e.g. '({value})'.

placeholder_contact.description: Stand-in contact used by --public builds and when private/contact.yaml is absent. Carries no real identity by construction.

cover_letter.description: Furniture a cover letter needs around the user's own prose. A profile's job_context.greeting / .closing override the first and last of these; fallback_salutee is reached only when job_context.hiring_manager is unset.

months.description: The twelve month names, January first. Written into the cover-letter date instead of strftime('%B'), which reads the C locale and is English whatever the project's locale says.

date_format.description: str.format template over {day}, {month} and {year}, e.g. '{month} {day}, {year}' or '{day} de {month} de {year}'. Separate from months so ordering is pack content rather than a branch in code.
